_about: WCAG 2.2 success criteria at levels A and AA, with the version each was introduced. 'auto' = how much an automated scan can decide: full (axe decides it reliably), partial (axe catches some failures; a human confirms the rest), manual (only a human can test it). 'plain' is for non-engineer readers of the report; 'test' is the manual check.

criteria.name: Non-text Content
criteria.plain: Images, icons and controls have a text alternative that says what they are or do.
criteria.test: With images off (or a screen reader), every meaningful image still makes sense; decorative images are silent.

criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.plain: Recorded audio has a transcript; silent video has a text or audio description.
criteria.test: Find each audio-only or video-only clip and confirm a transcript or description is linked beside it.

criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.plain: Recorded videos with sound have accurate captions.
criteria.test: Play each video with captions on; captions exist, are accurate and in sync, and name speakers.

criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.plain: Important visual information in videos is described in audio or text.
criteria.test: For each video, check that on-screen-only information (text, actions) is described.

criteria.name: Captions (Live)
criteria.plain: Live-streamed meetings and events have live captions.
criteria.test: Check that live streams (council meetings, briefings) offer real-time captions.

criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.plain: Recorded videos have an audio-described version where visuals carry meaning.
criteria.test: Confirm an audio-described track or version is available for videos whose visuals matter.

criteria.name: Info and Relationships
criteria.plain: Headings, lists, tables and form labels are built into the code, not just styled to look that way.
criteria.test: Screen reader heading list and table navigation match what is visually shown; form fields announce their labels.

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.plain: Content reads in a sensible order when styling is removed.
criteria.test: Read the page linearly with a screen reader; the order makes sense.

criteria.name: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.plain: Instructions don't rely only on shape, colour, size or position ("click the round green button").
criteria.test: Search instructions for words like left, right, round, red, above, below.

criteria.name: Orientation
criteria.plain: The site or app works in both portrait and landscape.
criteria.test: Rotate a phone; content is not locked to one orientation.

criteria.name: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.plain: Personal-info fields (name, email, address) are marked so browsers can autofill them.
criteria.test: Personal-data fields carry correct autocomplete values.

criteria.name: Use of Color
criteria.plain: Colour is never the only way to show meaning (errors, required fields, links).
criteria.test: View in greyscale; links, errors and statuses are still distinguishable.

criteria.name: Audio Control
criteria.plain: Audio that plays automatically can be paused or muted.
criteria.test: Any auto-playing audio over 3 seconds has a pause/stop/volume control.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.plain: Text is dark or light enough against its background to read (4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text).
criteria.test: Automated contrast check, plus text over images and gradients by hand.

criteria.name: Resize Text
criteria.plain: Text can be zoomed to 200% without losing content or function.
criteria.test: Browser zoom to 200%; nothing is cut off or overlapping.

criteria.name: Images of Text
criteria.plain: Real text is used instead of pictures of text (flyers posted as images are the common failure).
criteria.test: Look for flyers, banners and notices published as images.

criteria.name: Reflow
criteria.plain: At 400% zoom (a 320px-wide screen) the page fits without sideways scrolling.
criteria.test: Zoom to 400% at 1280px width; no horizontal scrolling for text content.

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.plain: Buttons, form borders, focus rings and chart elements have 3:1 contrast.
criteria.test: Measure input borders, icon buttons, focus indicators and chart segments.

criteria.name: Text Spacing
criteria.plain: Content still works when a reader increases line, letter and word spacing.
criteria.test: Apply a text-spacing bookmarklet; no text is clipped.

criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.plain: Tooltips and pop-ups can be dismissed and don't vanish while you're reading them.
criteria.test: Hover/focus tooltips: Esc dismisses, pointer can move onto them, they persist.

criteria.name: Keyboard
criteria.plain: Everything can be done with a keyboard alone.
criteria.test: Unplug the mouse; complete every key task (search, forms, menus, payments).

criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.plain: Keyboard users never get stuck inside a widget.
criteria.test: Tab through maps, embeds, modals and date pickers; you can always Tab or Esc out.

criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.plain: Single-letter shortcuts can be turned off or remapped.
criteria.test: Check for single-key shortcuts; they can be disabled or only work on focus.

criteria.name: Timing Adjustable
criteria.plain: Session time-outs warn you and let you extend.
criteria.test: Let a form or login sit; you are warned and can extend before losing work.

criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.plain: Carousels, animations and tickers can be paused.
criteria.test: Every auto-moving element has a pause control.

criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.plain: Nothing flashes more than three times a second.
criteria.test: Review animations and videos for flashing.

criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
criteria.plain: A "skip to main content" link or landmarks let people jump past repeated menus.
criteria.test: First Tab shows a working skip link, or the page has proper landmarks.

criteria.name: Page Titled
criteria.plain: Every page has a title that says what it is.
criteria.test: Browser tab titles are unique and descriptive.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.plain: Tabbing moves through the page in a logical order.
criteria.test: Tab through; focus follows the visual reading order and enters modals when they open.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.plain: Link text says where it goes (not "click here" or "read more").
criteria.test: List all links with a screen reader; each makes sense with its context.

criteria.name: Multiple Ways
criteria.plain: There is more than one way to find a page (search, site map, navigation).
criteria.test: Confirm site search or a site map exists alongside navigation.

criteria.name: Headings and Labels
criteria.plain: Headings and form labels describe the content or purpose.
criteria.test: Read the heading outline; it describes the page.

criteria.name: Focus Visible
criteria.plain: You can always see which element has keyboard focus.
criteria.test: Tab through; every focused element shows a clear indicator.

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.plain: Sticky headers, cookie banners and chat widgets don't hide the focused element.
criteria.test: Tab with banners and sticky bars showing; focus is never fully hidden.

criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
criteria.plain: Pinch, swipe and multi-finger gestures have a single-tap alternative.
criteria.test: Maps and carousels have buttons as well as gestures.

criteria.name: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.plain: Actions fire on release, so a mis-tap can be cancelled by sliding away.
criteria.test: Press a button, slide off, release; nothing fires.

criteria.name: Label in Name
criteria.plain: A control's spoken name contains its visible label, so voice control works.
criteria.test: Say the visible label with voice control; the control activates.

criteria.name: Motion Actuation
criteria.plain: Shake or tilt features have a button alternative.
criteria.test: Mobile: any motion-triggered action also has a control.

criteria.name: Dragging Movements
criteria.plain: Anything done by dragging can also be done with taps or clicks.
criteria.test: Sliders, sortable lists and map pins work without dragging.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.plain: Buttons and links are at least 24 by 24 pixels or well spaced.
criteria.test: Measure small icon buttons and dense link lists.

criteria.name: Language of Page
criteria.plain: The page declares its language so screen readers pronounce it correctly.
criteria.test: The html element has a valid lang attribute.

criteria.name: Language of Parts
criteria.plain: Passages in another language (e.g. Spanish content) are marked.
criteria.test: Mixed-language content carries lang attributes.

criteria.name: On Focus
criteria.plain: Moving focus never triggers a surprise page change.
criteria.test: Tabbing onto controls doesn't submit, navigate or open windows.

criteria.name: On Input
criteria.plain: Choosing an option doesn't unexpectedly submit or navigate.
criteria.test: Change dropdowns and radios; nothing happens until you confirm.

criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
criteria.plain: Navigation stays in the same place and order across pages.
criteria.test: Compare navigation across several pages.

criteria.name: Consistent Identification
criteria.plain: The same function is labelled the same way everywhere.
criteria.test: Search, print, login labels are consistent across pages.

criteria.name: Consistent Help
criteria.plain: Help (contact info, chat, FAQ) is in the same place on every page.
criteria.test: Help links appear in a consistent location.

criteria.name: Error Identification
criteria.plain: Form errors are described in text, not just a red border.
criteria.test: Submit forms with mistakes; each error is named in text and announced.

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.plain: Form fields have visible labels and needed instructions (formats, required fields).
criteria.test: Every field has a visible label; required fields and formats are stated.

criteria.name: Error Suggestion
criteria.plain: Error messages say how to fix the problem.
criteria.test: Error text suggests the correction ("Enter date as MM/DD/YYYY").

criteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.plain: Payments, applications and legal submissions can be reviewed, corrected or reversed.
criteria.test: Payment and application flows have a review step or undo.

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.plain: People aren't asked to re-type information they already gave in the same process.
criteria.test: Multi-step forms pre-fill or offer to reuse earlier answers.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.plain: Logging in doesn't require memorising or solving puzzles; paste and password managers work.
criteria.test: Login allows paste/autofill; CAPTCHA has a non-cognitive alternative.

criteria.name: Parsing
criteria.plain: Obsolete in WCAG 2.2 (always satisfied); still listed in 2.0/2.1 and Section 508.
criteria.test: Treated as satisfied per W3C errata; no separate test.

criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
criteria.plain: Custom controls (menus, tabs, toggles) tell assistive technology what they are and their state.
criteria.test: Screen reader announces each custom control's name, role and state.

criteria.name: Status Messages
criteria.plain: Messages like "3 results found" or "Saved" are announced without moving focus.
criteria.test: Trigger search, cart and save messages; a screen reader announces them.
